groups.title: Regularization and semipositive metrics
groups.summary: Locally bounded classical plurisubharmonic functions admit decreasing semipositive rational piecewise-linear approximations over the original field, on one fixed ordinary neighborhood. On smooth quasi-projective analytifications, continuous functions with positive CLD curvature admit smooth positive approximations on a fixed neighborhood, decreasing after shrinking. These two regularization results supply the bounded and continuous potential classes used in the product construction.
paragraphs: For an ample line bundle on a smooth projective variety admitting the stated regular model, curve positivity, CLD positivity and uniform Fubini–Study approximation are equivalent. The supporting results are contact rigidity, complete-intersection curve approximation and continuity and orthogonality of envelopes; the normal-model envelope theorem is recorded separately.
For rational integrable adelic line bundles with the specified identifications in the boundary completion, positive continuous local CLD curvature gives positive local mixed measures.

groups.title: Bounded products and independence of potentials
groups.summary: For a fixed positive closed background \(S\), the recursion \(T_{S,k}=d'd''(u_1T_{S,k-1})\) constructs positive closed mixed currents for locally bounded classical plurisubharmonic potentials. The products are symmetric, local and continuous under joint decreasing approximation, including a decreasing plurisubharmonic weight. They depend only on the curvature in each differentiated slot; consequently, products of currents with bounded classical local potentials glue.
paragraphs: Local Chern–Levine–Nirenberg estimates control the coefficient measures. Relations among degree-one curvature currents with continuous coefficients transfer to the product, and the operation extends continuously to the stated completion in the current-order norm.

The supporting calculus includes the specified piecewise-smooth differentials and finite étale formulas. For continuous current-positive potentials on smooth quasi-projective analytifications, locally uniform convergence of the potentials also permits weak convergence of the positive closed backgrounds.

groups.title: Capacity, quasicontinuity and comparison
groups.summary: Bounded classical potentials are locally quasicontinuous for the capacity defined by \(S\), and decreasing bounded approximations converge in that capacity. A compact boundary gap gives the relative comparison inequality and the stated domination conclusions modulo capacity zero. For the ambient background \(S=[1]\), local pluripolar, negligible and outer-capacity-null sets coincide; the Choquet and Borel regularity results hold on the specified exhaustion domains.
paragraphs: Closed restrictions to Borel parameter bands are constructed when the background is annihilated by the parameter differentials, with the stated disintegration hypotheses.

In the specified torus boxes with \(q=1\), outer capacity is inner regular on inverse images of Borel sets of finite \(\mathcal H^{n-1}\)-measure contained in a fixed compact moment subbox, for \(S_0=\beta^{n-1}[X]\) and backgrounds dominated by a constant multiple of \(S_0\) in current order.

proofLinks.label: Comparison with a compact boundary gap

groups.title: Unbounded products and finite energy
groups.summary: Truncation constructs non-polar products, separately closed whenever their coefficient masses are locally finite. On strict Laurent boxes with \(S\) extending past the closure, compact negative sublevels give an exact capacity-tail criterion for no loss of mass and a capacity characterization of every positive-power energy class. First energy admits a complete space of Borel representatives modulo relative outer-capacity zero, with intrinsic mixed currents and energies.
paragraphs: In this completion, strong convergence is exactly local truncated capacity convergence together with convergence of the energies. It gives the weighted-current limits up to the stated critical degree; mixed Green–Hölder has constant one.

The relative completed order also admits Perron envelopes, finite rooftops and the stated Borel obstacle problems. The unbounded calculus includes level currents and coarea formulas under their integrability hypotheses.

groups.title: Source equations and Dirichlet problems
groups.summary: On the stated Laurent domains, differences of completed first-energy potentials form a Banach space, and the nonlinear source map has norm-closed image. Every strongly continuous dual datum has a unique variational projection. For positive Radon data acting by bounded, strongly continuous actual integration, a nonnegative scalar defect of this projection vanishes exactly when the source equation has a solution; that solution is unique.
paragraphs: Fixed-source domination and the stated capacity bounds supply strong continuity of the actual integrals. Parameter and radial families, and small Hölder perturbations in specified smooth toric backgrounds with the required interface compatibility, give explicit source constructions.

Separately, when \(q=n-p=1\), a faithful regular strongly local coercive part form gives a unique renormalized zero-boundary solution for every finite signed energy-diffuse datum, with strong stability of fixed clippings. This is a linear equation in arbitrary ambient dimension.

openLinks.label: Strong integral continuity for general literal data

groups.title: Descent of analytic curvature relations
groups.summary: The constructed action respects degree-one relations and the specified constant-coefficient cycle relations. Quadratic relations descend for finite continuous closed-cell piecewise-linear or piecewise-smooth presentations whose joint residue rank is at most two, with no restriction on ambient dimension. Hence the quadratic action is canonical on germs of residue dimension at most two, including analytic surfaces. This is a statement about relations between expressions, beyond independence of individual potentials.
paragraphs: Higher action also descends on the ordinary-local weak closure of positive closed delta-backgrounds. Full-exact primitives, controlled approximations with one fixed positive current, and the stated carrier estimates provide proved sufficient criteria for descent.

For the specified model germs of residue dimension three, the action vanishes off the central point. It vanishes there below top degree; in top degree the remaining Dirac coefficient has an explicit spherical formula. Its general cancellation is the unresolved step.

proofLinks.label: Quadratic descent in rank at most two
Punctured action and the central residual

obstructions.summary: The counterexamples separate raw from outer relative capacity, refute relative strong subadditivity and the universal extremal total-mass formula, and show that the rooftop energy constant cannot always be one. Other examples force critical tail control and source compatibility: even small positive smooth density perturbations can leave the nonlinear source image. Further obstructions concern proposed primitive, gluing, lifting and duality arguments. The real finite-fan and critical-mass examples are not counterexamples to an actual analytic zero relation.

openObjectives.summary: The main remaining questions are descent of all analytic relations, critical central cancellation, Borel inner regularity for arbitrary relative outer capacities, strong continuity of general literal energy data, and conditions on a datum that ensure source compatibility. Full delta-test interfaces, larger domains and boundary classes, and classical representatives of completed potentials remain separate obligations.
